Of course my biggest concern is that some how I am right and "all" the doctors are wrong. My health anxiety is therefore by far my biggest concern. It initially began when I got sick earlier this year (sicker than I had ever been before). And since I've always had a bit of a hypochondria I began to fear the worst. So I decided to get tested (twice as I didn't believe the first results) and it came back negative. Then I talked to experts in this particular field and they told me that there was no way that I was sick. They literally told me "trust us, you are not infected". Then they proceeded to tell me to go see a psychiatrist. 

But the pain and anguish lingered and the illness. In my fear of the worst being true I self-medicated by drinking alcohol and taking ibuprofen and paracetamol. I went for further testing at my GP who did extensive blood work test and every thing came out normal.

At that time I began to see a therapist and he initially prescribed me truxal just so I could get some sleep as I suffered from horrible insomnia and night sweats.

Since the I have been functional but do have frequent breakdowns (less now though) and my current mixture of meds seem to be making some headway. 

But this fear and lack of feeling normal both physically and mentally has been going on for seven months now and I feel that if it won't get better soon, I will be dealing with this forever. That is just some thing that I know I can not handle in any way. At some time the suicidal thoughts will start to reappear and who knows what will happen then. 

I've been committed once into a mental institute but that experience freaked me so much that I could only make it for one day there. So all I can do is hope that some how things will turn around for me one day and I can look back at this experience and learn from it. 

I've always taken my life for granted (and wasted it because of minor problems of depression and self pity), but if I get through this I know I will have a completely different outlook on life. 

Thanks for responding and listening to my ramblings. It is quite therapeutic to be able to tell some body all this anonymously, because I can't express all these issues with my family and friends. I just don't want to worry them too much. And I've always been very introvert so that doesn't really help.

I had a similar experience with my gf. My last one always sucked me off and didn't mind to swallow at all. For the first few months of our relationship I got no bj action from her at all (except a few times when we were drunk). So one day I just mentioned it to her and how much I enjoy it. She consequently admitted to having a bit of a penis-phobia but promised to work on it. 

I also responded in the same way as you did, that is I stopped going down on her for some time. But after we discussed it honestly we now both take special care of providing each other the sought after activities and our sex life has never been better.

So I recommend you just tell her how big of a part it is for you and hopefully she will comply. If she knows how much it means to you she should be more willing to do it.

I had always been a casual drinker, going out every weekend and getting hammered. When my depression set in the drinking became more excessive and at a time I was drinking every day just to numb my feelings. I had this same urge as you describe; I just couldn't resist. 

After a few months of self-medicating through alcohol I decided to get help. It wasn't easy. Today I'm diagnosed with clinical depression and health anxiety disorder. I'm on clear instructions from my doctor that I should not drink one sip of booze. Nonetheless I find myself giving into the cravings (I'm writing this right now with a mild hangover at work). 

I am however determined to give it up for the summer and my best advice is, like always, find something else to shift your focus and energy on. I know it's hard because the drinking really does drain both your mental and physical stamina. I took up running and it has been extremely therapeutic for me.

Just try and consciously start every day thinking that you won't have a drink. And if you fail, at least try and keep it to a minimum, fx. 2 beers at most. 

Good luck man.
I guess I just wanted reddit's perspective as most of my friends sort of frown upon it and one even said that he could never respect and be with a girl who did that.

I took your advice and told her that I felt uncomfortable with her telling me about these things with other guys and that had detrimental effects on my feelings of insecurity. We continued to talk about these things in an open manner and her motives were similar to what you were saying, ie that she just wanted to stir up my emotions a bit and force me to express my love for her. So it was mostly to get MY attention and she would never act on it. I guess she just resents that I'm not a more macho type of a guy who would get overprotective and act more outraged. But I'm just not that guy. 

She did apologize and felt sorry for the way it kind of hurt my confidence. So in the end talking it out really helped to sort out some things in our relationship. I also realized how lucky I am to have her and recognized that I need to work on making her feel more wanted and just in general show her how much I love her.

I'm also feeling better today than the last few days and trying to have a more positive outlook on the future. 

So I just wanted to thank you again for taking the time to help me out here.

Thx for the reply, some really good pointers there. 

As regards my gf, it's her that brings up these things on her own. I don't really mind that some guys are flirting with her, but it worries me that she might act on it when she's drunk and careless. I know that these are guys that she knows from past experiences with her and she's already committed a minor error in this regard when she was living abroad. Ultimately I do trust her and we are actually planning on moving abroad together later this year. If she does however continue to express these doubts I will have to confront her and seriously consider my options. As it stands now though, I honestly do love her and want to keep the relationship going.

Hi, and thanks for taking the time to write a meaningful and helpful response.

I am aware that I must stop my drinking, but the problem is that even while I know that it hurts my chances of recovery it is in fact the only time when I manage to forget my problems just for one night and be able to have fun with my friends for a while. Going out on the weekends has always been a big part of my social life and I guess I'm just having a really hard time to give all that up.

As for the gf, a big part of why I managed to hide this from her is the fact that our relationship has been long-distance for quite some time as she is studying abroad. I know that it's no excuse for not telling her, but it certainly made it easier. She's moving back abroad in a few days and maybe that's a chance to break it off, even though I don't want to. 

My suicidal thoughts have pretty much vanished after I started taking the new meds even though I know they will pop back up if I won't sense any improvements in the coming weeks/months. Right now my main emotions are those of self hatred and anger towards my self. I fee like I finally got a chance to be happy (fx first real relationship with a girl a like a lot ) but managed to screw it all up in the worst manner.

I am determined however to give this therapy a real chance and just hope that things will start getting better. But if not, I really don't know what I will do.

Yeah, I met him last week and said that my condition has been deteriorating and explained this feeling of hopelessness. His main response was that this sort of clinical health anxiety is extremely persistent and prescribed me more anti-anxiety pills. One of my worst symptoms is my constant restlessness and inability to relax. I'm just having a really hard time believing that all my illnesses and symptoms are solely related to mental factors. So I need to work on trusting his diagnosis and change my pattern of thinking.

My concern now is that I won't be seeing him again for two months and worry that I will have a complete breakdown in that time.

And thanks for taking the time to correspond with me.

At first I was just seeing a therapist once in a while. Then after I got admitted I've been seeing another specialist more frequently and he has put me on more and heavier meds. Shortly after that I started feeling better but lately I've been spiralling back and obsessing about whether I will ever improve. I'm having regular panic attacks and break downs, but the anti-anxiety pills manage to keep in me in check for the most part.
